{{Quote|MI-series security droids were commonly used to guard upper-class civilian homes throughout the Empire.|A bounty posting on MI-726 describes the MI-series|<ref name="Gamer 6" />}}
'''MI-series security droids''' were a make of [[Security droid/Legends|security droid]] produced by [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]] during the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. At over two [[Meter/Legends|meter]]s tall they were armed with both [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blasters]] and short-range [[Stun blaster/Legends|stun blasters]]. Marketed to wealthy citizens and small planetary governments the model had a nearly two [[Standard year/Legends|year]] long waiting list a few years after its release.

==Characteristics==
The MI-series [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was a model of armed [[Security droid/Legends|Security droid]] manufactured by [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]]. They stood at just over two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall and were covered in [[Plasteel/Legends|plasteel]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]] manufactured to be resistant to heavy assault weapons. Of a quadrupedal design, the [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] were attached to the torso; the two heavy-duty hind legs ended in broad feet, while the front legs ended in a pair of massive, powerful hands with two fingers and an opposable thumb on each. The upper arms, attached at the shoulder, ended in a powerful weapon cluster.<ref name="Endless Vigil" /> Each cluster had a [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blaster]] and short-range [[Stun blaster/Legends|stun blaster]].<ref name="Gamer 6" />  

The droids were equipped with two large, [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] and a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]], that allowed them to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] in a deep, resonant tone. The MI-series had a humorless personality and were prone to barking orders and making bold declarations. They were programmed to invade the personal space of would-be trouble-makers in an attempt to intimidate before attacking. [[Memory wipe/Legends|Memory wipes]] were recommended to be conducted frequently to prevent the droids from developing a sadistic personality.<ref name="Endless Vigil" />

==History==
[[File:HolowanMechanicals.svg|thumb|right|150px|MI-series droid were manufactured by Holowan Mechanicals (logo pictured).]]
Designed by Holowan Mechanicals, the MI-series droid was released by the [[Imperial Era/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] into a crowded security droid market. The model was sold for 41,225 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] and its available weapons allowed the company to market the droid to wealthy civilians and small planetary governments. Within a few [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of its release the company had a nearly two year wait list for its MI-series.<ref name="Endless Vigil" /> [[MI-726]], one of the MI-series droid, went rogue after an [[Attack on a Sienar Fleet Systems board member's home|attack]] on its [[Unidentified Sienar Fleet Systems board member|owner's]] home and later resurfaced to attack various Imperial targets. A [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] of 100,000 credits was placed on the droid as a result.<ref name="Gamer 6" />

==Behind the scenes==
The MI-series was first mentioned as part of "[[Bounties to Die For]]," a [[2001]] article written by [[S. Mitch Ritchie]] and published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 6|sixth issue]] of [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine series.<ref name="Gamer 6" />
